## Optimization and Scaling Laws {#sec-ch3}

*Status: scaffold only — drafting has not yet begun for this chapter.*

**Purpose:** Cover AdamW-style optimization, learning-rate schedules,
and gradient-clipping/mixed-precision practicalities at scale, plus
compute-optimal scaling tradeoffs between model size, training-token
count, and compute budget.

**Planned subsections** (following `shared/chapter-template.qmd`'s
established structure):

- Learning objectives
- Why this matters
- Mental model or analogy
- Visual overview
- Technical core
- Worked example
- Compare and contrast
- Check your understanding
- Common misconception
- Applied exercise
- Interview lens
- Chapter recap
- Sources and further reading

**Source IDs this chapter will draw on:** [@src-50], [@src-51],
[@src-16].

**Boundary note:** Kaplan et al.'s scaling-law paper and Hoffmann et
al.'s Chinchilla paper must be taught together, not Chinchilla alone —
Chinchilla explicitly frames itself as reaching the same qualitative
conclusion as Kaplan et al. about not training to lowest possible loss,
while revising Kaplan et al.'s specific token/parameter scaling ratio.
Present this as a revision, not a contradiction, per Hoffmann et al.'s
own framing.
